ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, BD is the diagonal of rhombus ABCD with side length \(a\), where \( \angle BAD=60^\circ\). Points M and N start simultaneously from points A and B, respectively, moving towards points B and D at the same speed along AB and BD. Lines DM and AN are drawn and intersect at point P. Line BP is then drawn. What is the minimum value of BP?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $CD$ such that $CD=DG$,\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus, $\angle BAD=60^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADG=60^\circ$, $AD=GD$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADG$ is an equilateral triangle\\
In $\triangle ADM$ and $\triangle BAN$\\
$\because$ $\left\{\begin{array}{l}AD=BA\\ \angle DAM=\angle ABN=60^\circ\\ AM=BN\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADM\cong \triangle BAN\left(SAS\right)$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADM=\angle BAN$\\
$\because$ $\angle DAP+\angle BAN=60^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle GAD+\angle DAP+\angle GDA+\angle ADP=180^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ Points A, P, D, G are concyclic, the radius of the circle is $\frac{\frac{AD}{2}}{\cos30^\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}a}{3}$\\
$GB=2AB\cos30^\circ=\sqrt{3}a$\\
$\therefore$ When points G, P, B are collinear, namely when GP is the diameter of the circle, $BP$ is the shortest,\\
$\therefore$ $BP=GB−GP=\sqrt{3}a−2\times \frac{\sqrt{3}a}{3}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}a}{3}}$

method.method_draft: Synthetic locus method using an auxiliary equilateral triangle. From the diagram, identify A and B on the lower base, D above A, C above B, diagonal BD drawn, M on AB, N on BD, and P as the intersection of DM and AN with BP drawn. From the text, use that ABCD is a rhombus of side a, angle BAD is 60 degrees, and M and N move at the same speed, so AM = BN. Extend CD past D to a point G with DG = CD = a. Since the rhombus has angle BAD = 60 degrees, triangle ADG is equilateral. Compare triangles ADM and BAN: AD = BA, AM = BN, and the included angles are both 60 degrees, so they are congruent by SAS. Hence angle ADM = angle BAN. Since P lies on DM and AN, convert this angle relation into a cyclic condition showing A, P, D, G are concyclic. Thus P lies on the fixed circumcircle of equilateral triangle ADG, whose radius is a/sqrt(3). Compute GB = sqrt(3)a from the 30-60-90 geometry. The shortest BP occurs when B, P, G are collinear and GP is a diameter of the circle, so BP_min = GB - 2R = sqrt(3)a - 2a/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3)a/3.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中可见四边形 ABCD 为菱形，A 在左下，B 在右下，D 在左上，C 在右上；BD 是从 D 到 B 的对角线。M 在 AB 上，N 在 BD 上，DM 与 AN 相交于 P，并且从 B 向 P 作了线段 BP。

再推理：设菱形边长为 a，∠BAD=60°。因为 M、N 同时以相同速度分别从 A、B 出发，且 AB=BD=a，所以在同一时刻 AM=BN。

按辅助构造，延长 CD 过 D 到点 G，使 DG=CD=a。由于菱形中 AD=a，且 ∠BAD=60°，可得 ∠ADG=60°，又 AD=DG=a，所以 △ADG 是等边三角形。

比较 △ADM 与 △BAN：AD=BA=a，AM=BN，且 ∠DAM=∠ABN=60°，所以 △ADM≅△BAN（SAS）。因此 ∠ADM=∠BAN。

因为 P 在 DM 上，也在 AN 上，所以 ∠ADP=∠ADM，且 ∠DAP+∠BAN=60°。又 △ADG 为等边三角形，∠GAD=∠GDA=60°，于是
∠GAD+∠DAP+∠GDA+∠ADP=60°+∠DAP+60°+∠BAN=180°。
因此 A、P、D、G 四点共圆。这个圆是等边三角形 ADG 的外接圆，半径 R=a/√3=√3a/3。

由 30°-60°-90° 几何关系可得 GB=2a cos30°=√3a。点 P 在固定圆上运动，要使 BP 最小，P 应取圆上离 B 最近的点；此时 B、P、G 共线，且 GP 为该圆的直径，所以 GP=2R=2√3a/3。

因此 BP_min=GB-GP=√3a-2√3a/3=√3a/3。

再推理：设菱形边长为 a，∠BAD=60°。因为 M、N 同时以相同速度分别从 A、B 出发，且 AB=BD=a，所以在同一时刻 AM=BN。

按辅助构造，延长 CD 过 D 到点 G，使 DG=CD=a。由于菱形中 AD=a，且 ∠BAD=60°，可得 ∠ADG=60°，又 AD=DG=a，所以 △ADG 是等边三角形。

比较 △ADM 与 △BAN：AD=BA=a，AM=BN，且 ∠DAM=∠ABN=60°，所以 △ADM≅△BAN（SAS）。因此 ∠ADM=∠BAN。

因为 P 在 DM 上，也在 AN 上，所以 ∠ADP=∠ADM，且 ∠DAP+∠BAN=60°。又 △ADG 为等边三角形，∠GAD=∠GDA=60°，于是
∠GAD+∠DAP+∠GDA+∠ADP=60°+∠DAP+60°+∠BAN=180°。
因此 A、P、D、G 四点共圆。这个圆是等边三角形 ADG 的外接圆，半径 R=a/√3=√3a/3。

由 30°-60°-90° 几何关系可得 GB=2a cos30°=√3a。点 P 在固定圆上运动，要使 BP 最小，P 应取圆上离 B 最近的点；此时 B、P、G 共线，且 GP 为该圆的直径，所以 GP=2R=2√3a/3。

因此 BP_min=GB-GP=√3a-2√3a/3=√3a/3。

method.method_draft: Coordinate optimization method. From the diagram, set A and B as the horizontal lower side, D above-left, C above-right, with M moving on AB and N moving on diagonal BD; P is the intersection of DM and AN. From the text, because AB = AD = a and angle BAD = 60 degrees, triangle ABD is equilateral, so BD = a. Place coordinates A = (0,0), B = (a,0), D = (a/2, sqrt(3)a/2). Let s = AM/a = BN/a, with 0 <= s <= 1. Then M = (as,0), and since N divides BD from B to D in ratio s, N = (a(1 - s/2), sqrt(3)as/2). Write the line AN parametrically and the line DM parametrically, solve their intersection to get P as a function of s. This gives P = (a*s(1 - s/2)/(s^2 - s + 1), a*sqrt(3)*s^2/(2(s^2 - s + 1))). Compute BP^2 from these coordinates and simplify to BP^2 = a^2(3 - 2/(s^2 - s + 1)). Since s^2 - s + 1 has minimum 3/4 on [0,1] at s = 1/2, BP^2 is minimized there, giving BP_min = a/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3)a/3.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个菱形 ABCD，A 在左下，B 在右下，D 在左上，C 在右上；BD 是从 D 到 B 的对角线。点 M 位于 AB 上，点 N 位于 BD 上，线段 DM 与 AN 相交于 P，图中还画出了 BP。推理：因为 ABCD 是边长为 a 的菱形，且 ∠BAD = 60°，所以 AB = AD = a，并且三角形 ABD 为等边三角形，故 BD = a。按指定坐标法，取 A=(0,0), B=(a,0), D=(a/2, √3 a/2)。设 s = AM/a = BN/a，且 0 <= s <= 1。于是 M=(as,0)，N = B + s(D-B) = (a(1-s/2), √3 as/2)。设 P 在线 AN 上，则 P = uN = (u a(1-s/2), u √3 as/2)。又 P 在线 DM 上，则 P = D + v(M-D) = (a/2 + v(as-a/2), √3 a(1-v)/2)。由纵坐标相等得 us = 1-v，即 v=1-us。代入横坐标并约去 a：u(1-s/2)=1/2+(1-us)(s-1/2)=s-us(s-1/2)，所以 u[(1-s/2)+s(s-1/2)] = s，即 u(s^2-s+1)=s。令 q=s^2-s+1，则 u=s/q。故 P=(a s(1-s/2)/q, √3 a s^2/(2q))。于是 BP^2 = (x_P-a)^2 + y_P^2 = a^2[(s(1-s/2)/q - 1)^2 + 3s^4/(4q^2)] = a^2(3 - 2/q)。又 q=s^2-s+1=(s-1/2)^2+3/4，在 0 <= s <= 1 上最小值为 3/4，且 3 - 2/q 随 q 增大而增大，所以 BP^2 在 s=1/2 时最小。此时 BP_min^2 = a^2(3 - 2/(3/4)) = a^2/3，因此 BP_min = a/√3 = √3 a/3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, BD is the diagonal of rhombus ABCD with side length \(a\), where \(\angle BAD = 60^\circ\). Points M and N start simultaneously from points A and B, respectively, moving toward points B and D at the same speed along AB and BD. Lines DM and AN are drawn and intersect at point P. Then line BP is drawn. What is the minimum value of BP?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $CD$ such that $CD = DG$,\\
$\because$ quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus and $\angle BAD = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADG = 60^\circ$, $AD = GD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADG$ is an equilateral triangle.\\
In $\triangle ADM$ and $\triangle BAN$,\\
$\because$ $\left\{\begin{array}{l}AD = BA\\ \angle DAM = \angle ABN = 60^\circ\\ AM = BN\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADM \cong \triangle BAN\,(SAS)$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ADM = \angle BAN$.\\
$\because$ $\angle DAP + \angle BAN = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle GAD + \angle DAP + \angle GDA + \angle ADP = 180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ points A, P, D, G are concyclic, and the radius of the circle is $\frac{\frac{AD}{2}}{\cos 30^\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}a}{3}$.\\
$GB = 2AB\cos 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}a$.\\
$\therefore$ when points G, P, B are collinear, namely when $GP$ is the diameter of the circle, $BP$ is the shortest.\\
$\therefore$ $BP = GB - GP = \sqrt{3}a - 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}a}{3} = \boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}a}{3}}$

First describe the image: In the figure, it can be seen that quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, D is at the upper left, and C is at the upper right; BD is the diagonal from D to B. M is on AB, N is on BD, DM and AN intersect at P, and the line segment BP is drawn from B to P.

Then reason: Let the side length of the rhombus be a, and ∠BAD=60°. Because M and N set out from A and B respectively at the same speed at the same time, and AB=BD=a, at the same moment AM=BN.

According to the auxiliary construction, extend CD past D to point G, making DG=CD=a. Since in the rhombus AD=a, and ∠BAD=60°, it can be obtained that ∠ADG=60°; also AD=DG=a, so △ADG is an equilateral triangle.

Compare △ADM and △BAN: AD=BA=a, AM=BN, and ∠DAM=∠ABN=60°, so △ADM≅△BAN (SAS). Therefore ∠ADM=∠BAN.

Because P is on DM and also on AN, ∠ADP=∠ADM, and ∠DAP+∠BAN=60°. Also, △ADG is an equilateral triangle, ∠GAD=∠GDA=60°, hence
∠GAD+∠DAP+∠GDA+∠ADP=60°+∠DAP+60°+∠BAN=180°.
Therefore the four points A, P, D, G are concyclic. This circle is the circumcircle of the equilateral triangle ADG, with radius R=a/√3=√3a/3.

From the 30°-60°-90° geometric relationship, GB=2a cos30°=√3a can be obtained. Point P moves on the fixed circle; to make BP the smallest, P should be the point on the circle nearest to B; at this time B, P, G are collinear, and GP is the diameter of this circle, so GP=2R=2√3a/3.

Therefore BP_min=GB-GP=√3a-2√3a/3=√3a/3.
